title: 踏莎行·郴州旅舍
titleEn: Treading on Sedge · At an Inn in Chenzhou
author: 秦观
intro: Fog swallows the towers, the paradise of Peach Blossom Spring is nowhere to be found, and a cuckoo calls at dusk outside a lonely inn: one of the saddest lyrics an exiled Song poet ever wrote.
analysis: 这首词是秦观被贬到郴州（今湖南）时，在旅店里写的。上阕写景：大雾吞没了楼台，月色让渡口变得模糊，想找到传说中的世外桃源，却望穿眼睛也找不到。“桃源”出自陶渊明《桃花源记》，代表理想中没有烦恼的地方。怎么受得了一个人关在孤零零的旅馆里，春寒料峭，还在夕阳西下时听到杜鹃一声声啼叫！杜鹃的叫声像“不如归去”，最能引起思乡之情。下阕写远方亲友寄来梅花和书信，本是安慰，却一封封堆起来，像砌墙一样把愁“砌”得越来越高——把看不见的愁写成可以一块块砌起来的东西，非常新奇。结尾问郴江：你本来好好地绕着郴山流，为什么要流到潇湘去呢？表面问江，其实是问自己：我为什么会被冲到这么远的地方？据说苏轼特别喜欢这两句，把它写在扇子上。
analysisEn: Qin Guan wrote this at an inn in Chenzhou (in today’s Hunan) after being exiled there. The first stanza is landscape and mood: fog swallows the towers, moonlight blurs the ferry crossing, and he searches in vain for Peach Blossom Spring — the hidden paradise from Tao Yuanming’s famous story, a place free of trouble. How can he bear being shut in a lonely inn in the spring cold, hearing a cuckoo call as the sun goes down? The cuckoo’s cry was heard as “better go home”, the sound of homesickness itself. In the second stanza, friends send plum blossoms and letters from far away. They should comfort him, but they pile up instead, “building” his sorrow higher like bricks in a wall — a striking way to make a feeling solid. The ending asks the Chen River: you were happily circling Chen Mountain — for whom did you run off north to the Xiao and Xiang? He is really asking about himself: why was he swept so far from home? Su Shi is said to have loved these last two lines so much that he wrote them on his fan.
background: Qin Guan (1049–1100) was one of the “Four Scholars” who studied under Su Shi. Caught up in the factional struggles of the late Northern Song, he was exiled further and further south; he wrote this in Chenzhou around 1097 and died a few years later on his way back north.
pronunciation: 踏莎行 tà suō xíng（莎：莎草，不读 shā）；郴州 Chēnzhōu；可堪 kě kān；无重数 wú chóng shù；为谁 wèi shuí。机器朗读“郴、重、为”容易读错，已在“朗读用字”列换成同音字，音频需人工听验。
version: 采用通行文本（《淮海居士长短句》）。“雾失楼台，月迷津渡”无重要异文；“杜鹃声里斜阳暮”曾有人认为“斜阳”与“暮”意思重复，但通行本均作此。

lines.py: wù shī lóu tái, yuè mí jīn dù
lines.lit: Fog loses the towers; moonlight blurs the ferry crossing;
lines.en: The towers are lost in fog, the ferry blurred by the moon;

lines.py: táo yuán wàng duàn wú xún chù
lines.lit: I gaze for Peach Blossom Spring to the end — nowhere to find it.
lines.en: I strain my eyes for Peach Blossom Spring, but it is nowhere.

lines.py: kě kān gū guǎn bì chūn hán
lines.lit: How can I bear a lonely inn shut in the spring cold,
lines.en: How can I bear it — shut in a lonely inn against the spring cold,

lines.py: dù juān shēng lǐ xié yáng mù
lines.lit: the slanting sun at dusk amid the cuckoo’s cries?
lines.en: while the cuckoo calls and the last light dies?

lines.py: yì jì méi huā, yú chuán chǐ sù
lines.lit: By courier they send plum blossoms; by fish they pass letters on silk;
lines.en: Plum blossoms come by courier, letters come by fish —

lines.py: qì chéng cǐ hèn wú chóng shù
lines.lit: they pile up into this sorrow, layers beyond counting.
lines.en: each one a brick in a wall of sorrow, too high to count.

lines.py: chēn jiāng xìng zì rào chēn shān
lines.lit: The Chen River was happily circling Chen Mountain on its own —
lines.en: Chen River, you were content to wind around Chen Mountain —

lines.py: wèi shuí liú xià xiāo xiāng qù
lines.lit: for whom does it flow down to the Xiao and Xiang?
lines.en: so for whom did you run off to the Xiao and Xiang?

words.en: name of the tune (“Treading on Sedge”)
words.note: 莎：莎草，一种草，这里读 suō。
津：渡口。今天“天津”的“津”就是渡口的意思。

words.en: Peach Blossom Spring, a hidden paradise
words.note: 出自陶渊明《桃花源记》，今天“世外桃源”仍是常用成语。

words.en: to gaze until one can see no further

words.note: 现代汉语“不堪”“难堪”的“堪”，是“受得了”。
现代汉语既指杜鹃鸟，也指杜鹃花。
典故：南北朝陆凯折梅托驿使寄给朋友。驿：古代传递公文的站。
尺素：一尺长的白绢，代指书信。古人把信放在鱼形木函里，后来“鱼”成了书信的代称。
重：层，现代汉语“重重”“万重山”。

words.en: originally, as it should; happily on its own
words.note: 宋代口语，“本来好好地”，今天不用。
潇水、湘江，常代指湖南一带。

imagery.name: 杜鹃
imagery.zh: 黄昏时杜鹃一声声啼叫，像在说“不如归去”，让被贬在外的词人更加思乡、孤独。
imagery.en: At dusk the cuckoo keeps calling, as if saying “better go home” — deepening the exile’s homesickness and loneliness.

imagery.name: 夕阳
imagery.zh: 斜阳西下，一天又过去，孤馆里的人更觉凄凉。
imagery.en: The sun sinks and another day is gone; in the lonely inn the gloom grows heavier.

imagery.name: 梅
imagery.zh: 亲友寄来的梅花本是问候，却一层层堆成了愁。
imagery.en: Plum blossoms sent by friends should be a greeting, yet they pile up into sorrow.

imagery.name: 鱼
imagery.zh: “鱼传尺素”，鱼代表远方寄来的书信，信越多，越想家。
imagery.en: Fish stand for letters from afar; the more that arrive, the more he longs for home.
